question.problem:
The values of functions $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=-3$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $p(x)$ | $q(x)$ | $p'(x)$ | $q'(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-3$ | $1$ | $8$ | $0$ | $-2$ |

Compute $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big( p(x) + 5q(x) \big)$ at $x=-3.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left( p(x) + 5q(x) \right) = p'(x) + 5q'(x).
$$

At the point where $x=-3$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(p(x)+5q(x))|}_{x=-3} & ={p}^{′}(-3)+5{q}^{′}(-3) \\  & =0+5\cdot (-2) \\  & =-10.\end{aligned}
$$
